excerpt: By taking advantage of the sorting network theory, it is easy to model the network topology constraints through the notion of insertion network, or equivalently bubble network. As a consequence, the overall depth of the equivalent quantum circuit grows with the number n of logical qubits as 2n - 3 instead of a logarithmic log n depth factor as for classical sorting.
overview: This equation-like model explains why moving data qubits across a nearest-neighbor quantum network has different depth behavior from unconstrained classical sorting. It underpins the paper's data-qubit-swapping strategy without pretending that arbitrary pair swaps are free.
title: Sorting Network Depth Factor
